question: Will twitter / x.com be open source before September?
resolution_criteria:
[tweet]resolves YES if X publicly releases source covering the substantial core of the platform (backend serving, ranking, client apps), with narrow exclusions permitted for credentials, third-party proprietary dependencies, and genuinely security-sensitive modules — but NOT if the release is limited to the recommendation algorithm or another subsystem

Update 2026-07-27 (PST) (AI summary of creator comment): - The timezone used to determine when September begins is Central Daylight Time (CDT).
research:
I could not find any report, as of 2026-08-25, that X has published the core of its platform (backend serving, client apps). The only code released in August was another update to the recommendation algorithm repo, and the criteria explicitly say that does not count. Several page fetches failed at the proxy, so most items below come from search result summaries, not pages I read in full.

## 1. Resolution source
- No URL was given. The question resolves on whether X publicly releases source for the core of the platform before September begins in Central Daylight Time (CDT).
- The place to check is X's GitHub organizations. The only active repo I found is xai-org/x-algorithm, which holds the "For You" ranking code. I found no repo with backend serving or client app code. [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/x-open-sources-for-you-algorithm/)

## 2. Current status
- I found no evidence that anything close to the full codebase is out. The question is not settled, and all public releases so far are subsystems, which the criteria exclude.
- 2026-08-03: one report said the release "has not happened" because it is blocked on an internal security review with no firm completion date, and no license has been announced. [studioglobal](https://www.studioglobal.ai/discover/answers/search-fact-check-with-cited-sources-for-6a661fee6b10ab849409a67a)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-15: Musk posted "Any censorship required by governments is now clearly visible," tied to the open-source algorithm code. The repo includes a "Brazil2026ElectionFilter". [Brussels Signal](https://brusselssignal.eu/2026/08/elon-musk-says-x-will-make-government-censorship-requests-clearly-visible/), [X trending](https://x.com/i/trending/2089307368760955101), [@remarks](https://x.com/remarks/status/2088471384024392061)
- 2026-08-13/14: the X Open Source account pushed a new "For You" release to xai-org/x-algorithm under the Apache 2.0 license. It covers model configuration, filters and core ranking, reportedly 10 to 15 times bigger than the earlier release. X also launched an in-app shadowban checker. This is still only the ranking subsystem. [ETV Bharat](https://www.etvbharat.com/en/technology/x-algorithm-open-source-shadowban-transparency-tool-x-elon-musk-enn26081404733), [TechRound](https://techround.co.uk/business/x-just-open-sourced-its-algorithm-and-added-a-shadowban-checker-real-transparency-or-pr-theatre/), [X trending](https://x.com/i/trending/2087960858571792703)
- 2026-07-27: news outlets read Musk's posts as an August target for the full codebase. [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/07/27/x-to-open-source-full-codebase-in-august-musk-says/), [TechBriefly](https://techbriefly.com/2026/07/27/elon-musk-plans-to-open-source-xs-full-codebase/)
- 2026-07-24: Musk posted that "every line of code touching the 𝕏 system will be open source and third party audited next month." One aggregator phrased it as "every line of code running the X algorithm," which is ambiguous about scope. [Muskonomy](https://x.com/muskonomy/status/2081302742681923999)
- 2026-07-15: Musk said "We will make the entire codebase of X open source, with no exceptions," once a security vulnerability review is finished. Outside reviewers would check that the published code matches what runs in production. This came during a backlash over a Grok privacy breach. [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/x-open-source-codebase/), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/07/60492572/elon-musk-says-x-will-go-fully-open-source-with-no-exceptions-as-grok-faces-heat-over-privacy-breach-and-jailbreak-vulnerability), [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/x-open-source-codebase-musk/), [ProPakistani](https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/17/x-is-becoming-completely-open-source/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023-03: Twitter published part of its recommendation algorithm. Coverage says the promised updates never followed. [It's FOSS](https://itsfoss.com/news/x-might-be-going-open-source/), [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026)
- 2026-01: Musk said the new algorithm would be open-sourced "in a few days," and it did ship that month (xai-org/x-algorithm), with a major update in March. [AlternativeTo](https://alternativeto.net/news/2026/1/elon-musk-has-announced-he-will-open-source-x-s-new-algorithm-in-a-few-days), [Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/07/27/x-to-open-source-full-codebase-in-august-musk-says/)
- Musk has missed other open-source deadlines. For example, the promised Grok 3 weights did not appear on Hugging Face when the window closed. [byteiota](https://byteiota.com/x-is-open-sourcing-its-codebase-what-developers-need-to-know/), [explainx](https://www.explainx.ai/blog/x-open-source-entire-codebase-musk-july-2026)
- Pattern: Musk's open-source promises about the algorithm or subsystems have shipped, sometimes late. No major social platform has ever open-sourced its full production backend and client apps.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question or a close one, and no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The month Musk promised ends on 2026-08-31 (CDT). A full release, or a statement that it has slipped, could come in the last week.
- Things to watch:
  - Musk or @XOpenSource posts announcing the security review is done
  - New repos appearing under X or xai-org on GitHub
  - The named third-party auditors being announced
  - Any announced license
- Scope risk: a late-August release could again cover only the algorithm or "the X system" in a narrow sense, which would not meet the criteria.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - On 2026-07-15 Musk said "entire codebase... no exceptions."
  - On 2026-07-24 he said "every line of code touching the X system will be open source... next month."
  - X did ship a larger algorithm release on 2026-08-13/14, which shows some follow-through.
- For No:
  - 2026-08-03: the release was blocked on a security review with no date.
  - The mid-August release was only the ranking subsystem, which suggests the "X system" promise may be met narrowly.
  - No auditors, license or new repos have been announced as of 2026-08-25.
  - Sanitizing a huge production codebase in days is a large engineering task.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: August ends with no further release, or with another subsystem drop (for example the timeline or trust-and-safety code) that the criteria exclude. Musk says it is "coming soon."
- Yes: In the final week X drops a large set of repos (backend services, iOS/Android/web clients) with security-sensitive modules redacted, and the question creator judges it the substantial core.

(f) I start at about 7% for the reference class. I move down because of the short remaining window, the unresolved security review, and the lack of preparatory signals such as auditors, a license or new repos. I keep some weight for the chance of a surprise end-of-month dump that resolves generously. Final: about 3-4%.

Probability: 3%
